# Four-Bar Linkages {#chap-09-linkages}

```{r setup-09, include=FALSE}
## include the helpers.R file for pdf output of youtube on pdfs as a clickable link
source("R/helpers.R")
inject_jquery()
## include the required packages to make sure the page can be built.
source("R/required_packages.R")

## Set a consistent theme for all plots
theme_linkage <- theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 12 * chart_text_scale, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 10 * chart_text_scale),
    axis.text = element_blank(),
    axis.title = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks = element_blank(),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA)
  )

## Four-bar position solver: ground pivots O2 = (0, 0) and O4 = (g, 0), input angle t2 (rad).
## Returns A and B (open branch: B on the left of the line from A to O4), or NULL if the loop cannot close.
fourbar <- function(a, b, c, g, t2, branch = 1) {
  A <- c(a * cos(t2), a * sin(t2)); O4 <- c(g, 0)
  d <- sqrt(sum((O4 - A)^2))
  if (d > b + c || d < abs(b - c)) return(NULL)
  ex <- (O4 - A) / d; ey <- c(-ex[2], ex[1])
  x <- (b^2 - c^2 + d^2) / (2 * d); h <- sqrt(max(b^2 - x^2, 0))
  B <- A + x * ex + branch * h * ey
  list(A = A, B = B)
}
## Circle / arc as a data frame (angles in rad)
arc_df <- function(cx, cy, r, from = 0, to = 2 * pi, n = 100) {
  t <- seq(from, to, length.out = n); data.frame(x = cx + r * cos(t), y = cy + r * sin(t))
}
## Ground hatching under a pivot
hatch <- function(x, y, w = 0.5) {
  xs <- seq(x - w, x + w, length.out = 6)
  list(annotate("segment", x = x - w, xend = x + w, y = y - 0.12, yend = y - 0.12, linewidth = 0.8),
       annotate("segment", x = xs, xend = xs - 0.15, y = y - 0.12, yend = y - 0.32, linewidth = 0.5))
}
## Draw one linkage position (ground pivots at (0,0) and (g,0))
draw_fb <- function(p, g, lt = "solid", alpha = 1, lw = 3) list(
  annotate("segment", x = 0, y = 0, xend = p$A[1], yend = p$A[2], linewidth = lw, color = "steelblue", linetype = lt, alpha = alpha, lineend = "round"),
  annotate("segment", x = p$A[1], y = p$A[2], xend = p$B[1], yend = p$B[2], linewidth = lw, color = "orange", linetype = lt, alpha = alpha, lineend = "round"),
  annotate("segment", x = g, y = 0, xend = p$B[1], yend = p$B[2], linewidth = lw, color = "forestgreen", linetype = lt, alpha = alpha, lineend = "round"),
  annotate("point", x = c(p$A[1], p$B[1]), y = c(p$A[2], p$B[2]), size = 3.5, shape = 21, fill = "white", stroke = 1.2, alpha = alpha))
pivots <- function(g) list(hatch(0, 0), hatch(g, 0),
  annotate("point", x = c(0, g), y = c(0, 0), size = 4.5, shape = 21, fill = "white", stroke = 1.5))
```

## Learning Objectives {#sec-objectives-09}

By the end of this chapter, you will be able to:

1. **Identify** the components and terminology of four-bar linkage mechanisms
2. **Apply** Grashof's Law to classify four-bar linkages
3. **Distinguish** between crank-rocker, double-crank, rocker-crank, double-rocker and triple-rocker mechanisms
4. **Analyze** linkage motion using position analysis techniques
5. **Select** appropriate linkage configurations for specific motion requirements

::: {.callout-think}
**Before You Read:** When you open a car hood, the hinges guide it through a specific path—rising up and forward—rather than just swinging in a simple arc. What mechanism might be hidden in the hinge to produce this carefully designed motion?
:::

## Introduction to Four-Bar Linkages {#sec-linkages-intro}

The **four-bar linkage** is one of the most fundamental and versatile mechanisms in mechanical engineering. Despite its apparent simplicity—just four rigid links connected by four revolute (pin) joints—it can produce an extraordinary variety of motions. Four-bar linkages are found in countless applications, from automobile suspensions to robotic arms, from aircraft landing gear to simple hand tools.

A four-bar linkage converts **rotary motion** into complex **output motion** that can be:

1. **Another rotation** (with variable angular velocity)
2. **Oscillating motion** (back-and-forth rotation)
3. **Complex path motion** (coupler curves)

***

> **Think About It:** When you open a car hood, the hinges guide it through a specific path—rising up and forward—rather than just swinging in a simple arc. This carefully designed motion comes from a four-bar linkage hidden in the hinge mechanism!

***

## Anatomy of a Four-Bar Linkage {-}

A four-bar linkage consists of four rigid members (links) connected in a closed loop by four revolute joints (pins).

```{r four-bar-anatomy, echo=FALSE, fig.width=10, fig.height=7, fig.align='center', fig.cap="Components of a four-bar linkage mechanism."}
## Define the four-bar linkage positions
## Ground pivots
O2 <- c(2, 2)     ## Input crank pivot (fixed)
O4 <- c(8, 2)     ## Output rocker pivot (fixed)

## Moving pivots (example position)
A <- c(3.5, 4)    ## Connection between crank and coupler
B <- c(7, 4.5)    ## Connection between coupler and rocker

ggplot() +
  ## Ground (link 1) - shown as hatched/fixed
  geom_segment(aes(x = O2[1], xend = O4[1], y = O2[2], yend = O4[2]),
               linewidth = 3, color = "gray40") +
  ## Ground hatching
  geom_segment(aes(x = seq(1.5, 8.5, 0.5), xend = seq(1.2, 8.2, 0.5),
                   y = rep(2, 15), yend = rep(1.6, 15)),
               linewidth = 0.5, color = "gray40") +

  ## Input crank (link 2)
  geom_segment(aes(x = O2[1], xend = A[1], y = O2[2], yend = A[2]),
               linewidth = 4, color = "steelblue") +

  ## Coupler (link 3)
  geom_segment(aes(x = A[1], xend = B[1], y = A[2], yend = B[2]),
               linewidth = 4, color = "orange") +

  ## Output rocker (link 4)
  geom_segment(aes(x = O4[1], xend = B[1], y = O4[2], yend = B[2]),
               linewidth = 4, color = "forestgreen") +

  ## Fixed pivots (ground joints)
  geom_point(aes(x = c(O2[1], O4[1]), y = c(O2[2], O4[2])),
             size = 8, color = "black") +
  geom_point(aes(x = c(O2[1], O4[1]), y = c(O2[2], O4[2])),
             size = 5, color = "white") +
  geom_point(aes(x = c(O2[1], O4[1]), y = c(O2[2], O4[2])),
             size = 2, color = "black") +

  ## Moving pivots
  geom_point(aes(x = c(A[1], B[1]), y = c(A[2], B[2])),
             size = 7, color = "black") +
  geom_point(aes(x = c(A[1], B[1]), y = c(A[2], B[2])),
             size = 4, color = "white") +

  ## Labels for links
  annotate("text", x = 5, y = 1.3, label = "Ground (Link 1) - Fixed",
           fontface = "bold", size = 3.5 * diagram_text_scale, color = "gray40") +
  annotate("text", x = 2.2, y = 3.3, label = "Input Crank\n(Link 2)",
           fontface = "bold", size = 3.5 * diagram_text_scale, color = "steelblue") +
  annotate("text", x = 5.2, y = 5, label = "Coupler (Link 3)",
           fontface = "bold", size = 3.5 * diagram_text_scale, color = "darkorange") +
  annotate("text", x = 8.9, y = 4.6, hjust = 0, label = "Output\nRocker\n(Link 4)",
           fontface = "bold", size = 3.5 * diagram_text_scale, color = "forestgreen") +

  ## Labels for pivots
  annotate("text", x = O2[1], y = O2[2] - 0.6, label = "O2", fontface = "bold", size = 4 * diagram_text_scale) +
  annotate("text", x = O4[1], y = O4[2] - 0.6, label = "O4", fontface = "bold", size = 4 * diagram_text_scale) +
  annotate("text", x = A[1] - 0.5, y = A[2] + 0.3, label = "A", fontface = "bold", size = 4 * diagram_text_scale) +
  annotate("text", x = B[1] + 0.5, y = B[2] + 0.3, label = "B", fontface = "bold", size = 4 * diagram_text_scale) +

  ## Length labels
  annotate("text", x = 5, y = 2.4, label = "g (ground)", size = 3 * diagram_text_scale, fontface = "italic") +
  annotate("text", x = 2.4, y = 2.9, label = "a", size = 3 * diagram_text_scale, fontface = "italic") +
  annotate("text", x = 5.3, y = 4.1, label = "b", size = 3 * diagram_text_scale, fontface = "italic") +
  annotate("text", x = 7.8, y = 3, label = "c", size = 3 * diagram_text_scale, fontface = "italic") +

  ## Input/Output arrows
  geom_curve(aes(x = 2, xend = 2.8, y = 1.2, yend = 1.6),
             arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.15, "cm"), type = "closed"),
             curvature = 0.3, linewidth = 1, color = "red") +
  annotate("text", x = 2.5, y = 0.9, label = "Input\nMotion", color = "red", size = 3 * diagram_text_scale) +

  geom_curve(aes(x = 8.7, xend = 8.2, y = 3, yend = 3.8),
             arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.15, "cm"), type = "closed"),
             curvature = -0.3, linewidth = 1, color = "purple") +
  annotate("text", x = 9.3, y = 3.5, label = "Output\nMotion", color = "purple", size = 3 * diagram_text_scale) +

  ## Legend box
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = 0.5, xmax = 4.5, ymin = 5.5, ymax = 7.5),
            fill = "white", color = "black") +
  annotate("text", x = 2.5, y = 7.2, label = "LINK TERMINOLOGY", fontface = "bold", size = 3.5 * diagram_text_scale) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = 0.7, xend = 1.3, y = 6.7, yend = 6.7), linewidth = 3, color = "gray40") +
  annotate("text", x = 1.5, y = 6.7, label = "Ground (frame)", size = 2.8 * diagram_text_scale, hjust = 0) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = 0.7, xend = 1.3, y = 6.3, yend = 6.3), linewidth = 3, color = "steelblue") +
  annotate("text", x = 1.5, y = 6.3, label = "Input (crank/rocker)", size = 2.8 * diagram_text_scale, hjust = 0) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = 0.7, xend = 1.3, y = 5.9, yend = 5.9), linewidth = 3, color = "orange") +
  annotate("text", x = 1.5, y = 5.9, label = "Coupler (floating link)", size = 2.8 * diagram_text_scale, hjust = 0) +

  coord_fixed(ratio = 1, xlim = c(0, 10), ylim = c(0.5, 8)) +
  labs(title = "Four-Bar Linkage Anatomy") +
  theme_linkage
```

**Key Components:**

| Component | Symbol | Description |
|:----------|:-------|:------------|
| **Ground (Link 1)** | $g$ | Fixed link connecting the two ground pivots |
| **Input Link (Link 2)** | $a$ | Driven by motor or actuator; connected to ground at O2 |
| **Coupler (Link 3)** | $b$ | "Floating" link connecting the two moving pivots |
| **Output Link (Link 4)** | $c$ | Delivers output motion; connected to ground at O4 |
| **Ground Pivots** | O2, O4 | Fixed pivot points attached to the frame |
| **Moving Pivots** | A, B | Pivot points that move during operation |

***

## Grashof's Law {-}

**Grashof's Law** determines whether a four-bar linkage can achieve continuous rotation or is limited to oscillating (rocking) motion. This is the most fundamental criterion for classifying four-bar linkages.

### The Grashof Criterion {-}

For a four-bar linkage with link lengths $a$, $b$, $c$, and $g$:

$$S + L \leq P + Q$$

**Where:**

| Symbol | Definition |
|:-------|:-----------|
| $S$ | Length of the **shortest** link |
| $L$ | Length of the **longest** link |
| $P$ | Length of one remaining link |
| $Q$ | Length of the other remaining link |

***

### Classification by Grashof Condition {-}

```{r grashof-classification, echo=FALSE, fig.width=10, fig.height=8, fig.align='center', fig.cap="Classification of four-bar linkages based on Grashof's Law. For a Grashof linkage, the position of the shortest link decides the type."}
box <- function(x0, x1, y0, y1, title, lines, fill, tsize = 3) list(
  annotate("rect", xmin = x0, xmax = x1, ymin = y0, ymax = y1, fill = fill, color = "black"),
  annotate("text", x = (x0 + x1) / 2, y = y1 - 0.4, label = title, fontface = "bold", size = tsize * diagram_text_scale),
  annotate("text", x = (x0 + x1) / 2, y = (y0 + y1) / 2 - 0.25, label = lines, size = 2.4 * diagram_text_scale, lineheight = 1.1))

ggplot() +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 3.5, xmax = 8.5, ymin = 9, ymax = 10.5, fill = "steelblue", color = "black") +
  annotate("text", x = 6, y = 10, label = "GRASHOF'S LAW", fontface = "bold", size = 5 * diagram_text_scale, color = "white") +
  annotate("text", x = 6, y = 9.4, label = "S + L  vs  P + Q", size = 4 * diagram_text_scale, color = "white") +
  annotate("segment", x = c(6, 3, 3, 9.5), xend = c(6, 9.5, 3, 9.5), y = c(9, 8, 8, 8), yend = c(8, 8, 7, 7), linewidth = 1) +
  box(0.6, 5.4, 5.6, 7, "GRASHOF", "S + L < P + Q\nat least one link turns fully", "lightgreen", 4) +
  box(7.4, 11.6, 5.6, 7, "NON-GRASHOF", "S + L > P + Q", "lightyellow", 4) +
  annotate("segment", x = c(3, -0.3, -0.3, 1.9, 4.1, 6.3), xend = c(3, 6.3, -0.3, 1.9, 4.1, 6.3),
           y = c(5.6, 4.9, 4.9, 4.9, 4.9, 4.9), yend = c(4.9, 4.9, 4.4, 4.4, 4.4, 4.4), linewidth = 0.5) +
  box(-1.3, 0.7, 1.9, 4.4, "Crank-Rocker", "Shortest = input\nInput: full turn\nOutput: rocks", "palegreen") +
  box(0.9, 2.9, 1.9, 4.4, "Double-Crank", "Shortest = ground\nInput: full turn\nOutput: full turn", "palegreen") +
  box(3.1, 5.1, 1.9, 4.4, "Rocker-Crank", "Shortest = output\nInput: rocks\nOutput: full turn", "palegreen") +
  box(5.3, 7.3, 1.9, 4.4, "Double-Rocker", "Shortest = coupler\nInput and output\nrock; the coupler\nturns fully", "palegreen") +
  annotate("segment", x = 9.5, xend = 9.5, y = 5.6, yend = 4.4, linewidth = 0.5) +
  box(8, 11, 1.9, 4.4, "Triple-Rocker", "No link turns fully\nAll links rock", "moccasin") +
  box(2.5, 9.5, 0.2, 1.5, "SPECIAL CASE: S + L = P + Q", "Change-point mechanism: the links line up (dead points)", "lavender") +
  coord_fixed(ratio = 1, xlim = c(-1.5, 12), ylim = c(0, 10.8)) +
  theme_void()
```

### Grashof Classification Summary {-}

```{r grashof-table, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE}
grashof_types <- tribble(
  ~Type, ~Condition, ~Shortest_Link, ~Input_Motion, ~Output_Motion, ~Application,
  "Crank-Rocker", "S + L < P + Q", "Input link (a)", "Continuous rotation", "Oscillation", "Windshield wipers, pumps",
  "Double-Crank", "S + L < P + Q", "Ground (g)", "Continuous rotation", "Continuous rotation", "Drag-link quick-return, rotary feeders",
  "Rocker-Crank", "S + L < P + Q", "Output link (c)", "Oscillation", "Continuous rotation", "Treadle drives (sewing machine, lathe)",
  "Double-Rocker", "S + L < P + Q", "Coupler (b)", "Oscillation", "Oscillation", "Aircraft landing gear, Ackermann steering",
  "Triple-Rocker", "S + L > P + Q", "Any", "Oscillation only", "Oscillation only", "Rocking mechanisms"
)

grashof_types %>%
  kbl(caption = "Four-Bar Linkage Classification by Grashof Condition",
      col.names = c("Type", "Condition", "Shortest Link", "Input", "Output", "Example Applications"),
      booktabs = TRUE) %>%
  kable_styling(latex_options = c("hold_position", "scale_down"), full_width = knitr::is_html_output()) %>%
  row_spec(0, background = "#D81B60", color = "white") %>%
  row_spec(1:4, background = "#E8F5E9") %>%
  row_spec(5, background = "#FFF3E0")
```

## Types of Four-Bar Linkages {-}

### Crank-Rocker Mechanism {-}

The **crank-rocker** is the most common four-bar linkage configuration. The input link (crank) rotates continuously while the output link (rocker) oscillates back and forth.

```{r crank-rocker, echo=FALSE, fig.width=10, fig.height=6, fig.align='center', fig.cap="Crank-rocker mechanism (a = 1.2, b = 4, c = 3, g = 4.5) drawn in three positions computed from the loop closure: the crank turns fully (dashed circle) while the rocker swings between its two limit positions."}
a <- 1.2; b <- 4; c <- 3; g <- 4.5
t2 <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 721)
th4 <- sapply(t2, function(t) { p <- fourbar(a, b, c, g, t); atan2(p$B[2], p$B[1] - g) })
rng <- range(th4)
p1 <- fourbar(a, b, c, g, 60 * pi / 180); p2 <- fourbar(a, b, c, g, 170 * pi / 180); p3 <- fourbar(a, b, c, g, 290 * pi / 180)
swing <- diff(rng) * 180 / pi

ggplot() +
  geom_path(data = arc_df(0, 0, a), aes(x, y), linetype = "dashed", color = "steelblue") +
  geom_path(data = arc_df(g, 0, c, rng[1], rng[2]), aes(x, y), color = "forestgreen", linewidth = 1,
            arrow = arrow(ends = "both", length = unit(0.2, "cm"), type = "closed")) +
  draw_fb(p2, g, "dashed", 0.55, 2) + draw_fb(p3, g, "dotted", 0.7, 2) + draw_fb(p1, g) +
  pivots(g) +
  annotate("text", x = -1.5, y = 0.9, label = "Crank:\nfull 360°", color = "steelblue", fontface = "bold", size = 3.2 * diagram_text_scale) +
  annotate("text", x = g + 1.9, y = 2.2, label = sprintf("Rocker:\nswings %.0f°", swing), color = "forestgreen", fontface = "bold", size = 3.2 * diagram_text_scale) +
  annotate("text", x = g / 2, y = -0.6, label = "Ground (link 1)", color = "gray40", size = 3 * diagram_text_scale) +
  annotate("label", x = 1, y = 4.6, label = "Applications: windshield wipers,\nfans that oscillate, agitators", size = 2.9 * diagram_text_scale, fill = "lightyellow", hjust = 0) +
  coord_fixed(xlim = c(-2.3, 7.6), ylim = c(-1.6, 5.2)) +
  labs(title = "Crank-Rocker") +
  theme_linkage
```

***

### Double-Crank (Drag-Link) Mechanism {-}

In a **double-crank** or **drag-link** mechanism, both the input and output links can rotate continuously. This occurs when the **ground link is the shortest**.

```{r double-crank, echo=FALSE, fig.width=10, fig.height=6, fig.align='center', fig.cap="Double-crank (drag-link) mechanism (g = 1.2 shortest, a = 3, b = 3.5, c = 3.2): both the input and the output make full turns (dashed circles), the output at a non-uniform speed."}
a <- 3; b <- 3.5; c <- 3.2; g <- 1.2
p1 <- fourbar(a, b, c, g, 70 * pi / 180); p2 <- fourbar(a, b, c, g, 230 * pi / 180)
ggplot() +
  geom_path(data = arc_df(0, 0, a), aes(x, y), linetype = "dashed", color = "steelblue") +
  geom_path(data = arc_df(g, 0, c), aes(x, y), linetype = "dashed", color = "forestgreen") +
  draw_fb(p2, g, "dashed", 0.55, 2) + draw_fb(p1, g) +
  pivots(g) +
  annotate("text", x = -3.9, y = 2.4, label = "Input crank:\nfull 360°", color = "steelblue", fontface = "bold", size = 3.2 * diagram_text_scale) +
  annotate("text", x = 5.3, y = 2.4, label = "Output crank:\nfull 360°", color = "forestgreen", fontface = "bold", size = 3.2 * diagram_text_scale) +
  annotate("text", x = g / 2, y = -0.7, label = "Ground = shortest link", color = "gray40", fontface = "italic", size = 3 * diagram_text_scale) +
  annotate("label", x = -5.5, y = -3.3, label = "Key feature: non-uniform output\nspeed from a uniform input", size = 2.9 * diagram_text_scale, fill = "lightgreen", hjust = 0) +
  annotate("label", x = 3.0, y = -3.3, label = "Applications: drag-link quick-return\n(shapers), rotary feeders", size = 2.9 * diagram_text_scale, fill = "lightyellow", hjust = 0) +
  coord_fixed(xlim = c(-5.6, 7.4), ylim = c(-4, 4.4)) +
  labs(title = "Double-Crank (Drag-Link)") +
  theme_linkage
```

***

### Triple-Rocker (Non-Grashof) {-}

When the Grashof condition is **not satisfied** ($S + L > P + Q$), no link can complete a full revolution. All links are restricted to oscillating (rocking) motion.

```{r triple-rocker, echo=FALSE, fig.width=10, fig.height=5.5, fig.align='center', fig.cap="Triple-rocker mechanism (a = 2.6, b = 3, c = 2.8, g = 4; non-Grashof): the input can only swing through a limited range (arc), and so can the output."}
a <- 2.6; b <- 3; c <- 2.8; g <- 4
t2 <- seq(-pi, pi, length.out = 2001)
ok <- sapply(t2, function(t) !is.null(fourbar(a, b, c, g, t)))
t_ok <- t2[ok]; lim <- range(t_ok)                     # input range on the open branch (one continuous interval)
th4 <- sapply(t_ok, function(t) { p <- fourbar(a, b, c, g, t); atan2(p$B[2], p$B[1] - g) %% (2 * pi) })   # 0..2pi: no wrap for this linkage
pm <- fourbar(a, b, c, g, 60 * pi / 180)
pl <- fourbar(a, b, c, g, lim[2] - 0.01)
ggplot() +
  geom_path(data = arc_df(0, 0, a, lim[1], lim[2]), aes(x, y), color = "steelblue", linewidth = 1,
            arrow = arrow(ends = "both", length = unit(0.2, "cm"), type = "closed")) +
  geom_path(data = arc_df(g, 0, c, min(th4), max(th4)), aes(x, y), color = "forestgreen", linewidth = 1,
            arrow = arrow(ends = "both", length = unit(0.2, "cm"), type = "closed")) +
  draw_fb(pl, g, "dashed", 0.55, 2) + draw_fb(pm, g) +
  pivots(g) +
  annotate("text", x = -2.6, y = 1.2, label = sprintf("Input swings\n%.0f° only", diff(lim) * 180 / pi), color = "steelblue", fontface = "bold", size = 3.2 * diagram_text_scale) +
  annotate("text", x = g + 2.6, y = 1.6, label = sprintf("Output swings\n%.0f°", diff(range(th4)) * 180 / pi), color = "forestgreen", fontface = "bold", size = 3.2 * diagram_text_scale) +
  annotate("label", x = g / 2, y = -1.6, label = "S + L = 2.6 + 4 = 6.6 > P + Q = 2.8 + 3 = 5.8:\nno continuous rotation possible",
           size = 3 * diagram_text_scale, fill = "mistyrose", color = "darkred") +
  coord_fixed(xlim = c(-3.6, 7.6), ylim = c(-2.3, 3.8)) +
  labs(title = "Triple-Rocker (Non-Grashof)") +
  theme_linkage
```

***

## Position Analysis {-}

Position analysis determines the configuration of a linkage for a given input angle. This is fundamental for understanding linkage motion and for design.

### Loop Closure Equation {-}

The four-bar linkage forms a closed vector loop:

$$\vec{a} + \vec{b} = \vec{g} + \vec{c}$$

In component form (x and y):

$$a \cos\theta_2 + b \cos\theta_3 = g + c \cos\theta_4$$
$$a \sin\theta_2 + b \sin\theta_3 = c \sin\theta_4$$

```{r vector-loop, echo=FALSE, fig.width=10, fig.height=6, fig.align='center', fig.cap="Vector loop closure for position analysis: a + b = g + c, with all angles measured counter-clockwise from the ground line."}
a <- 1.6; b <- 4; c <- 3; g <- 4.5
p <- fourbar(a, b, c, g, 65 * pi / 180)
t3 <- atan2(p$B[2] - p$A[2], p$B[1] - p$A[1]); t4 <- atan2(p$B[2], p$B[1] - g)
va <- arrow(length = unit(0.3, "cm"), type = "closed")
ggplot() +
  annotate("segment", x = 0, y = 0, xend = p$A[1], yend = p$A[2], arrow = va, linewidth = 1.6, color = "steelblue") +
  annotate("segment", x = p$A[1], y = p$A[2], xend = p$B[1], yend = p$B[2], arrow = va, linewidth = 1.6, color = "darkorange") +
  annotate("segment", x = g, y = 0, xend = p$B[1], yend = p$B[2], arrow = va, linewidth = 1.6, color = "forestgreen") +
  annotate("segment", x = 0, y = 0, xend = g, yend = 0, arrow = va, linewidth = 1.6, color = "purple") +
  ## reference lines and angle arcs
  annotate("segment", x = p$A[1], xend = p$A[1] + 1.4, y = p$A[2], yend = p$A[2], linetype = "dotted") +
  annotate("segment", x = g, xend = g + 1.3, y = 0, yend = 0, linetype = "dotted") +
  geom_path(data = arc_df(0, 0, 0.7, 0, 65 * pi / 180), aes(x, y), color = "steelblue") +
  geom_path(data = arc_df(p$A[1], p$A[2], 0.9, 0, t3), aes(x, y), color = "darkorange") +
  geom_path(data = arc_df(g, 0, 0.6, 0, t4), aes(x, y), color = "forestgreen") +
  annotate("text", x = 0.95, y = 0.35, label = "theta[2]", parse = TRUE, color = "steelblue", size = 4 * diagram_text_scale) +
  annotate("text", x = p$A[1] + 1.2, y = p$A[2] + 0.22, label = "theta[3]", parse = TRUE, color = "darkorange", size = 4 * diagram_text_scale) +
  annotate("text", x = g + 0.85, y = 0.45, label = "theta[4]", parse = TRUE, color = "forestgreen", size = 4 * diagram_text_scale) +
  annotate("text", x = p$A[1] / 2 - 0.35, y = p$A[2] / 2 + 0.1, label = "a", fontface = "bold", size = 5 * diagram_text_scale, color = "steelblue") +
  annotate("text", x = (p$A[1] + p$B[1]) / 2, y = (p$A[2] + p$B[2]) / 2 + 0.35, label = "b", fontface = "bold", size = 5 * diagram_text_scale, color = "darkorange") +
  annotate("text", x = (g + p$B[1]) / 2 + 0.35, y = p$B[2] / 2, label = "c", fontface = "bold", size = 5 * diagram_text_scale, color = "forestgreen") +
  annotate("text", x = g / 2, y = -0.35, label = "g", fontface = "bold", size = 5 * diagram_text_scale, color = "purple") +
  annotate("text", x = c(-0.3, g + 0.1, p$A[1] - 0.3, p$B[1]), y = c(-0.3, -0.35, p$A[2] + 0.25, p$B[2] + 0.35),
           label = c("O2", "O4", "A", "B"), fontface = "bold", size = 4 * diagram_text_scale) +
  annotate("label", x = 0.3, y = 3.8, label = "Loop closure:  a + b = g + c", fontface = "bold.italic", size = 3.8 * diagram_text_scale, hjust = 0) +
  coord_fixed(xlim = c(-1, 6.3), ylim = c(-0.8, 4.3)) +
  labs(title = "Vector Loop for Four-Bar Position Analysis") +
  theme_linkage
```

### Freudenstein's Equation {-}

**Freudenstein's Equation** provides a relationship between input angle $\theta_2$ and output angle $\theta_4$:

$$K_1 \cos\theta_4 - K_2 \cos\theta_2 + K_3 = \cos(\theta_2 - \theta_4)$$

**Where:**

$$K_1 = \frac{g}{a}, \quad K_2 = \frac{g}{c}, \quad K_3 = \frac{a^2 - b^2 + c^2 + g^2}{2ac}$$

This equation is particularly useful for **function generation** problems, where a specific input-output relationship is desired.

***

## Transmission Angle {-}

The **transmission angle** ($\mu$) is the angle between the coupler and the output link. It is a critical measure of linkage quality—how effectively force is transmitted through the mechanism.

```{r transmission-angle, echo=FALSE, fig.width=10, fig.height=6, fig.align='center', fig.cap="Transmission angle: the angle mu at B between the coupler and the output link (linkage a = 40, b = 90, c = 70, g = 100 mm at theta2 = 60 deg)."}
a <- 40; b <- 90; c <- 70; g <- 100
p <- fourbar(a, b, c, g, 60 * pi / 180)
uBA <- atan2(p$A[2] - p$B[2], p$A[1] - p$B[1]); uBO <- atan2(-p$B[2], g - p$B[1])
mu <- acos(cos(uBA - uBO)) * 180 / pi
## arc between the two link directions at B (take the short way round)
d <- (uBO - uBA + pi) %% (2 * pi) - pi
ggplot() +
  draw_fb(p, g, lw = 3) + pivots(g) +
  geom_path(data = arc_df(p$B[1], p$B[2], 14, uBA, uBA + d), aes(x, y), color = "red", linewidth = 1.3) +
  annotate("text", x = p$B[1] + 20 * cos(uBA + d / 2), y = p$B[2] + 20 * sin(uBA + d / 2),
           label = sprintf("mu == %.0f*degree", mu), parse = TRUE, color = "red", size = 4.5 * diagram_text_scale) +
  annotate("text", x = c(-5, g + 5, p$A[1] - 5, p$B[1] + 5), y = c(-6, -6, p$A[2] + 5, p$B[2] + 6),
           label = c("O2", "O4", "A", "B"), fontface = "bold", size = 4 * diagram_text_scale) +
  annotate("label", x = 115, y = 40, hjust = 0, size = 3 * diagram_text_scale, fill = "white",
           label = "DESIGN GUIDELINES\nIdeal: mu = 90 deg\nGood: 40 deg < mu < 140 deg\nAvoid: mu near 0 or 180 deg\n(dead point: no torque on the output)") +
  coord_fixed(xlim = c(-15, 190), ylim = c(-12, 85)) +
  labs(title = "Transmission Angle in a Four-Bar Linkage") +
  theme_linkage
```

### Transmission Angle Formula {-}

The transmission angle can be calculated using the **law of cosines**:

$$\cos\mu = \frac{b^2 + c^2 - (a^2 + g^2 - 2ag\cos\theta_2)}{2bc}$$

**Design Rules:**

| Transmission Angle | Quality | Recommendation |
|:-------------------|:--------|:---------------|
| $\mu = 90°$ | Optimal | Maximum force transmission |
| $40° < \mu < 140°$ | Good | Acceptable for most applications |
| $30° < \mu < 150°$ | Marginal | May need stronger components |
| $\mu < 30°$ or $\mu > 150°$ | Poor | Avoid—high forces, poor motion quality |

***

## Coupler Curves {-}

One of the most powerful features of four-bar linkages is the ability to generate complex curves using a point attached to the coupler link. These **coupler curves** can approximate straight lines, circles, or other complex shapes.

```{r coupler-curve-concept, echo=FALSE, fig.width=10, fig.height=7, fig.align='center', fig.cap="Coupler point P, fixed to the coupler, traces a coupler curve as the crank turns (crank-rocker a = 1.5, b = 4, c = 3, g = 5)."}
a <- 1.5; b <- 4; c <- 3; g <- 5
p_dist <- 2.5; p_angle <- 0.6           # P relative to A: distance and angle from the line A -> B
cpt <- function(p) { u <- atan2(p$B[2] - p$A[2], p$B[1] - p$A[1]) + p_angle; p$A + p_dist * c(cos(u), sin(u)) }
curve <- t(sapply(seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 361), function(t) cpt(fourbar(a, b, c, g, t))))
curve <- data.frame(x = curve[, 1], y = curve[, 2])
p <- fourbar(a, b, c, g, 60 * pi / 180); P <- cpt(p)
ggplot() +
  geom_path(data = curve, aes(x, y), linewidth = 1.6, color = "red", alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_polygon(aes(x = c(p$A[1], p$B[1], P[1]), y = c(p$A[2], p$B[2], P[2])), fill = "orange", alpha = 0.35, color = "orange") +
  draw_fb(p, g) + pivots(g) +
  annotate("point", x = P[1], y = P[2], size = 4, shape = 21, fill = "red", stroke = 1.2) +
  annotate("text", x = P[1] - 0.3, y = P[2] + 0.3, label = "P", fontface = "bold", size = 5 * diagram_text_scale, color = "red") +
  annotate("text", x = -2.4, y = 4.2, label = "Coupler curve:\npath traced by P", color = "red", size = 3.3 * diagram_text_scale, hjust = 0) +
  annotate("text", x = 5.3, y = 2.4, label = "Coupler (link 3) carries\nthe coupler point P", color = "darkorange", size = 3 * diagram_text_scale, hjust = 0) +
  coord_fixed(xlim = c(-2.5, 8.8), ylim = c(-1.6, 5.4)) +
  labs(title = "Coupler Curve") +
  theme_linkage
```

## Applied Example: Grashof Classification {#linkage-example-1}

::: {.question}
##### Problem Statement {-}

A four-bar linkage has the following link lengths:

- Link 1 (ground): $g = 100$ mm
- Link 2 (input): $a = 40$ mm
- Link 3 (coupler): $b = 90$ mm
- Link 4 (output): $c = 70$ mm

Determine:

1. Whether this is a Grashof or non-Grashof linkage
2. The type of mechanism (crank-rocker, double-crank, etc.)
3. Which link should be the input for continuous rotation

:::

::: {.answer}
##### Solution {-}


::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
*This one is live — change any of the four link lengths below and the mechanism is reclassified immediately.*

```{r calc-grashof-interactive, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
qwebr_calc_card(
  label = "grashof-interactive",
  title = "Grashof Condition Calculator",
  icon = "gears",
  inputs = list(
    qwebr_calc_input("g", "Ground link g", value = 100, min = 10, max = 300, step = 1, suffix = "mm"),
    qwebr_calc_input("a", "Input link a", value = 40, min = 10, max = 300, step = 1, suffix = "mm"),
    qwebr_calc_input("b", "Coupler link b", value = 90, min = 10, max = 300, step = 1, suffix = "mm"),
    qwebr_calc_input("c", "Output link c", value = 70, min = 10, max = 300, step = 1, suffix = "mm")
  ),
  goal = "Turn the crank-rocker into a Grashof double-crank by changing only the ground link g (leave a = 40, b = 90 and c = 70 mm).",
  goal_test = "mech_type == \"Double-Crank\" && SL < PQ && a == 40 && b == 90 && c == 70",
  mode = "task")
```

<details class="qwebr-calc-source">
<summary>Show the live R code behind this calculator</summary>
<p>The card above re-runs this exact webR code every time you change an input, substituting your values for the variables at the top. Edit the code directly and press <strong>Run Code</strong> to experiment further.</p>

```{webr-r}
#| label: grashof-interactive
## Given link lengths (mm) - edit these and re-run!
g <- 100  ## ground
a <- 40   ## input
b <- 90   ## coupler
c <- 70   ## output

## Sort to find S (shortest) and L (longest)
links <- c(a, b, c, g)
link_names <- c("a (input)", "b (coupler)", "c (output)", "g (ground)")
sorted_idx <- order(links)

S <- links[sorted_idx[1]]
S_name <- link_names[sorted_idx[1]]
L <- links[sorted_idx[4]]
L_name <- link_names[sorted_idx[4]]
P <- links[sorted_idx[2]]
Q <- links[sorted_idx[3]]

## Grashof check
SL <- S + L
PQ <- P + Q
is_grashof <- SL <= PQ

## Determine mechanism type
if (is_grashof) {
  if (S_name == "g (ground)") {
    mech_type <- "Double-Crank"
  } else if (S_name == "a (input)") {
    mech_type <- "Crank-Rocker"
  } else if (S_name == "c (output)") {
    mech_type <- "Rocker-Crank"
  } else {
    mech_type <- "Double-Rocker"
  }
} else {
  mech_type <- "Triple-Rocker (Non-Grashof)"
}

if (SL < PQ) {
  grashof_class <- "S + L < P + Q: GRASHOF"
} else if (SL == PQ) {
  grashof_class <- "S + L = P + Q: CHANGE POINT"
} else {
  grashof_class <- "S + L > P + Q: NON-GRASHOF"
}

## Print the results
cat("Mechanism type:", mech_type, "\n")
cat(sprintf("  Shortest link (S)    %g mm - %s\n", S, S_name))
cat(sprintf("  Longest link (L)     %g mm - %s\n", L, L_name))
cat(sprintf("  S + L                %g mm\n", SL))
cat(sprintf("  P + Q                %g mm\n", PQ))
cat(sprintf("  Grashof condition    %s\n", grashof_class))

## Interpretation
if (is_grashof) {
  if (S_name == "a (input)") {
    cat("The shortest link is the input: it rotates continuously while the output oscillates.\n")
  } else if (S_name == "g (ground)") {
    cat("The shortest link is the ground: both the input and the output rotate continuously.\n")
  } else if (S_name == "c (output)") {
    cat("The shortest link is the output: it rotates continuously while the input oscillates.\n")
  } else {
    cat("The shortest link is the coupler: both the input and the output only oscillate.\n")
  }
} else {
  cat("No link can complete a full rotation - all links merely rock.\n")
}
```

</details>
:::

::: {.content-visible unless-format="html"}
```{r grashof-example-calc, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE}
## Given link lengths
g <- 100  ## ground
a <- 40   ## input
b <- 90   ## coupler
c <- 70   ## output

## Sort to find S and L
links <- c(a, b, c, g)
link_names <- c("a (input)", "b (coupler)", "c (output)", "g (ground)")
sorted_idx <- order(links)

S <- links[sorted_idx[1]]
S_name <- link_names[sorted_idx[1]]
L <- links[sorted_idx[4]]
L_name <- link_names[sorted_idx[4]]
P <- links[sorted_idx[2]]
Q <- links[sorted_idx[3]]

## Grashof check
SL <- S + L
PQ <- P + Q

is_grashof <- SL <= PQ

## Determine mechanism type
if (is_grashof) {
  if (S_name == "g (ground)") {
    mech_type <- "Double-Crank"
  } else if (S_name == "a (input)") {
    mech_type <- "Crank-Rocker"
  } else if (S_name == "c (output)") {
    mech_type <- "Rocker-Crank"
  } else {
    mech_type <- "Double-Rocker"
  }
} else {
  mech_type <- "Triple-Rocker (Non-Grashof)"
}

## Create results table
results <- tribble(
  ~Step, ~Calculation, ~Result,
  "Step 1: Identify shortest (S)", paste0("S = min(", a, ", ", b, ", ", c, ", ", g, ")"), paste0(S, " mm (", S_name, ")"),
  "Step 2: Identify longest (L)", paste0("L = max(", a, ", ", b, ", ", c, ", ", g, ")"), paste0(L, " mm (", L_name, ")"),
  "Step 3: Calculate S + L", paste0("S + L = ", S, " + ", L), paste0(SL, " mm"),
  "Step 4: Calculate P + Q", paste0("P + Q = ", P, " + ", Q), paste0(PQ, " mm"),
  "Step 5: Compare (Grashof test)", paste0("S + L (", SL, ") vs P + Q (", PQ, ")"),
  ifelse(SL < PQ, "S + L < P + Q: GRASHOF", ifelse(SL == PQ, "S + L = P + Q: CHANGE POINT", "S + L > P + Q: NON-GRASHOF")),
  "Step 6: Mechanism type", "Based on shortest link position", mech_type
)

results %>%
  kbl(caption = "Grashof Classification Example",
      booktabs = TRUE,
      col.names = c("Step", "Calculation", "Result")) %>%
  kable_styling(latex_options = "hold_position", full_width = knitr::is_html_output()) %>%
  row_spec(0, background = "#D81B60", color = "white") %>%
  row_spec(5, background = "#E8F5E9", bold = TRUE) %>%
  row_spec(6, background = "#E3F2FD", bold = TRUE)
```

##### Interpretation {-}

- Since $S + L$ (`r SL` mm) is less than $P + Q$ (`r PQ` mm), this is a **Grashof linkage**. (With $b = 80$ and $c = 60$ mm the two sums would be equal, 140 = 140: a change-point linkage that locks up in a straight line once per turn.)
- The shortest link is the **input link (a = `r a` mm)**.
- When the shortest link is the input (crank), the mechanism is a **Crank-Rocker**.
- The input (link 2) will rotate continuously while the output (link 4) oscillates.
:::
:::

## Applied Example: Transmission Angle Analysis {#linkage-example-2}

::: {.question}
##### Problem Statement {-}


For the linkage in the previous example (a = 40, b = 90, c = 70, g = 100 mm), calculate the transmission angle when the input is at:

1. $\theta_2 = 60°$
2. Determine the minimum transmission angle through the full rotation

:::

::: {.answer}
##### Solution {-}


::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
*This one is live — change any of the four link lengths below and the transmission-angle curve, the results, and the design-quality verdict update immediately.*

```{r calc-trans-angle-interactive, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
qwebr_calc_card(
  label = "trans-angle-interactive",
  title = "Transmission Angle Calculator",
  icon = "gears",
  inputs = list(
    qwebr_calc_input("a", "Input link a", value = 40, min = 10, max = 300, step = 1, suffix = "mm", type = "slider"),
    qwebr_calc_input("b", "Coupler link b", value = 90, min = 10, max = 300, step = 1, suffix = "mm", type = "slider"),
    qwebr_calc_input("c", "Output link c", value = 70, min = 10, max = 300, step = 1, suffix = "mm", type = "slider"),
    qwebr_calc_input("g", "Ground link g", value = 100, min = 10, max = 300, step = 1, suffix = "mm", type = "slider")
  ),
  mode = "demo")
```

<details class="qwebr-calc-source">
<summary>Show the live R code behind this calculator</summary>
<p>The card above re-runs this exact webR code every time you change an input, substituting your values for the variables at the top. Edit the code directly and press <strong>Run Code</strong> to experiment further.</p>

```{webr-r}
#| label: trans-angle-interactive
## Given link lengths (mm) - edit these and re-run!
a <- 40   ## input link
b <- 90   ## coupler
c <- 70   ## output link
g <- 100  ## ground link

## Function to calculate transmission angle
calc_trans_angle <- function(theta2, a, b, c, g) {
  ## Convert to radians
  t2 <- theta2 * pi / 180

  ## Calculate diagonal (distance from O4 to A)
  ## Using law of cosines
  diag_sq <- a^2 + g^2 - 2*a*g*cos(t2)

  ## Transmission angle using law of cosines
  cos_mu <- (b^2 + c^2 - diag_sq) / (2*b*c)

  ## Clamp to valid range
  cos_mu <- max(-1, min(1, cos_mu))

  mu <- acos(cos_mu) * 180 / pi
  return(mu)
}

## Calculate for theta2 = 60 deg
mu_60 <- calc_trans_angle(60, a, b, c, g)

## Find min and max through full rotation
theta2_range <- seq(0, 360, by = 1)
mu_values <- sapply(theta2_range, calc_trans_angle, a = a, b = b, c = c, g = g)
mu_min <- min(mu_values, na.rm = TRUE)
mu_max <- max(mu_values, na.rm = TRUE)
theta_at_min <- theta2_range[which.min(mu_values)]

## Transmission angle over one full input rotation, minimum marked
par(mar = c(5, 5, 3, 1), cex.main = 1.3, cex.lab = 1.2, cex.axis = 1.1)
plot(theta2_range, mu_values, type = "l", lwd = 4, col = "#2c3e50", ylim = c(0, 180),
     xlab = "Input angle theta2 (deg)", ylab = "Transmission angle mu (deg)",
     main = "Transmission Angle over One Input Rotation", las = 1, xaxt = "n")
axis(1, at = seq(0, 360, by = 90))
abline(h = 40, lty = 2, col = "#bdc3c7")
points(theta_at_min, mu_min, pch = 19, cex = 2.2, col = "#e74c3c")

## Design quality verdict
if (mu_min > 40 && mu_max < 140) {
  cat("Design Quality: GOOD\n")
  advice <- "Transmission angle stays between 40 and 140 deg - acceptable design"
} else if (mu_min > 30 && mu_max < 150) {
  cat("Design Quality: MARGINAL\n")
  advice <- "Consider redesigning for better force transmission"
} else {
  cat("Design Quality: !!POOR!!\n")
  advice <- "Redesign required - excessive joint forces at minimum transmission angle"
}

## Print the results
cat(sprintf("  Transmission angle at theta2 = 60 deg  %.1f deg\n", mu_60))
cat(sprintf("  Minimum transmission angle             %.1f deg (at theta2 = %g deg)\n", mu_min, theta_at_min))
cat(sprintf("  Maximum transmission angle             %.1f deg\n", mu_max))
cat(advice, "\n")
```

</details>
:::

::: {.content-visible unless-format="html"}
```{r trans-angle-example, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE}
## Given
a <- 40
b <- 90
c <- 70
g <- 100

## Function to calculate transmission angle
calc_trans_angle <- function(theta2, a, b, c, g) {
  ## Convert to radians
  t2 <- theta2 * pi / 180

  ## Calculate diagonal (distance from O4 to A)
  ## Using law of cosines
  diag_sq <- a^2 + g^2 - 2*a*g*cos(t2)

  ## Transmission angle using law of cosines
  cos_mu <- (b^2 + c^2 - diag_sq) / (2*b*c)

  ## Clamp to valid range
  cos_mu <- max(-1, min(1, cos_mu))

  mu <- acos(cos_mu) * 180 / pi
  return(mu)
}

## Calculate for theta2 = 60 deg
mu_60 <- calc_trans_angle(60, a, b, c, g)

## Find min and max through full rotation
theta2_range <- seq(0, 360, by = 1)
mu_values <- sapply(theta2_range, calc_trans_angle, a = a, b = b, c = c, g = g)
mu_min <- min(mu_values, na.rm = TRUE)
mu_max <- max(mu_values, na.rm = TRUE)
theta_at_min <- theta2_range[which.min(mu_values)]

## Results table
trans_results <- tribble(
  ~Parameter, ~Formula, ~Value,
  "At theta2 = 60 deg", "cos(mu) = (b^2 + c^2 - f^2) / 2bc", paste0(round(mu_60, 1), " deg"),
  "Minimum transmission angle", "Through full crank rotation", paste0(round(mu_min, 1), " deg"),
  "Maximum transmission angle", "Through full crank rotation", paste0(round(mu_max, 1), " deg"),
  "Input angle at min mu", "theta2 where mu is minimum", paste0(round(theta_at_min, 1), " deg")
)

trans_results %>%
  kbl(caption = "Transmission Angle Analysis",
      booktabs = TRUE,
      col.names = c("Parameter", "Formula/Description", "Value")) %>%
  kable_styling(latex_options = "hold_position", full_width = knitr::is_html_output()) %>%
  row_spec(0, background = "#D81B60", color = "white") %>%
  row_spec(2, background = ifelse(mu_min > 40, "#E8F5E9", "#FFEBEE"), bold = TRUE)
```

##### Quality Assessment {-}

```{r quality-assessment, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE}
if (mu_min > 40 && mu_max < 140) {
  quality <- "GOOD"
  recommendation <- "Transmission angle stays between 40 and 140 deg - acceptable design"
  color <- "darkgreen"
} else if (mu_min > 30 && mu_max < 150) {
  quality <- "MARGINAL"
  recommendation <- "Consider redesigning for better force transmission"
  color <- "orange"
} else {
  quality <- "POOR"
  recommendation <- "Redesign required - excessive joint forces at minimum transmission angle"
  color <- "red"
}
```

**Design Quality:** `r quality`

**Recommendation:** `r recommendation`
:::
:::

## Try it yourself {#sec-tryit-fourbar}

These use linkages that are not in the worked examples. Each exercise checks your answer and lets you try again.

### Classify eight linkages {#sec-tryit-grashof-sort}

```{r tryit-grashof-sort, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
gs <- data.frame(g = c(100, 30, 100, 100, 120, 100, 55, 90),
                 a = c(30, 80, 80, 90, 50, 60, 70, 100),
                 b = c(90, 90, 90, 25, 110, 70, 90, 120),
                 c = c(70, 70, 30, 80, 80, 80, 100, 20))
gs_class <- function(g, a, b, c) {
  links <- c(g = g, a = a, b = b, c = c)
  o <- order(links)
  S <- links[o[1]]; L <- links[o[4]]; PQ <- sum(links[o[2:3]])
  if (S + L > PQ) return("Triple-rocker (non-Grashof)")
  switch(names(S), a = "Crank-rocker", g = "Double-crank", c = "Rocker-crank", b = "Double-rocker")
}
gs$bin <- mapply(gs_class, gs$g, gs$a, gs$b, gs$c)
stopifnot(all(vapply(seq_len(nrow(gs)), function(i) {
  l <- unlist(gs[i, c("g", "a", "b", "c")]); o <- sort(l); o[1] + o[4] != o[2] + o[3]
}, logical(1))))   # no change-point cases

tryit_sort(
  id = "grashof-sort",
  title = "What kind of four-bar is it?",
  bins = c("Crank-rocker", "Double-crank", "Rocker-crank", "Double-rocker", "Triple-rocker (non-Grashof)"),
  cards = data.frame(
    text = sprintf("Ground %d, input %d, coupler %d, output %d mm", gs$g, gs$a, gs$b, gs$c),
    bin = gs$bin,
    why = vapply(seq_len(nrow(gs)), function(i) {
      l <- c(Ground = gs$g[i], Input = gs$a[i], Coupler = gs$b[i], Output = gs$c[i])
      o <- order(l)
      sprintf("S + L = %d + %d = %d; P + Q = %d + %d = %d. Shortest link: %s.",
              l[o[1]], l[o[4]], l[o[1]] + l[o[4]], l[o[2]], l[o[3]], l[o[2]] + l[o[3]], names(l)[o[1]])
    }, character(1))
  ),
  intro = "Find S, L, P and Q first, then use the position of the shortest link.",
  question = paste0(
    "<p>For each four-bar linkage find the shortest link S and the longest link L, and compare S + L with P + Q. ",
    "If S + L is greater, the linkage is a triple-rocker (non-Grashof). Otherwise the shortest link decides: input - crank-rocker, ",
    "ground - double-crank, output - rocker-crank, coupler - double-rocker. None of the cases is a change point.</p>")
)
```

### Transmission angle {#sec-tryit-trans-angle}

A four-bar has input $a = 35$ mm, coupler $b = 85$ mm, output $c = 65$ mm and ground $g = 95$ mm. The input is at $\theta_2 = 75^\circ$.

```{r tryit-trans-number, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
ta <- list(a = 35, b = 85, c = 65, g = 95, th = 75)
ta$diag2 <- ta$a^2 + ta$g^2 - 2 * ta$a * ta$g * cos(ta$th * pi / 180)
ta$cosmu <- (ta$b^2 + ta$c^2 - ta$diag2) / (2 * ta$b * ta$c)
ta$mu    <- acos(ta$cosmu) * 180 / pi

tryit_number(
  id = "trans-angle",
  title = "Transmission angle at 75 degrees",
  answers = list(
    tryit_answer("Diagonal squared a^2 + g^2 - 2 a g cos(theta_2)", ta$diag2, tol = 5, suffix = "mm2",
                 hint = "Use cos(75 degrees) = 0.2588. Square the link lengths first."),
    tryit_answer("cos(mu)", ta$cosmu, tol = 0.002,
                 hint = "(b^2 + c^2 - diagonal^2) / (2 b c)."),
    tryit_answer("Transmission angle mu", ta$mu, tol = 0.3, suffix = "degrees",
                 hint = "mu = arccos(cos mu), in degrees.")
  ),
  intro = "Then judge it against the chapter's table of transmission-angle quality.",
  question = paste0(
    "<p>A four-bar linkage has input link a = 35 mm, coupler b = 85 mm, output c = 65 mm and ground g = 95 mm. ",
    "At input angle theta_2 = 75 degrees: cos(mu) = (b&sup2; + c&sup2; - (a&sup2; + g&sup2; - 2 a g cos(theta_2))) / (2 b c).</p>")
)
```

<details class="tryit-solution">
<summary>Show the worked solution</summary>

$$d^2 = 35^2 + 95^2 - 2 \cdot 35 \cdot 95 \cos 75^\circ = `r sprintf("%.0f", ta$diag2)` \text{ mm}^2$$

$$\cos\mu = \frac{85^2 + 65^2 - `r sprintf("%.0f", ta$diag2)`}{2 \cdot 85 \cdot 65} = `r sprintf("%.3f", ta$cosmu)`, \qquad \mu = `r sprintf("%.1f", ta$mu)`^\circ$$

That is within the "good" band (40 to 140 degrees) at this crank angle; the minimum over a full rotation still has to be checked.

</details>

## Design Guidelines {-}

### Link Length Selection {-}

| Design Goal | Guideline |
|:------------|:----------|
| **Continuous crank rotation** | Ensure Grashof condition: $S + L \leq P + Q$ |
| **Crank-rocker mechanism** | Make the input link the shortest |
| **Good transmission angle** | Keep $\mu_{min} > 40°$ throughout motion |
| **Avoid toggle positions** | Transmission angle should not approach 0° or 180° |
| **Symmetrical output** | Consider time ratio requirements |

### Time Ratio {-}

The **time ratio** (TR) describes how the output motion is divided between forward and return strokes:

$$TR = \frac{\text{Time for forward stroke}}{\text{Time for return stroke}} = \frac{\alpha}{\beta}$$

Where $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are the crank angles for forward and return strokes.

For a **quick-return mechanism**, TR > 1, meaning the return stroke is faster than the forward stroke.

***

## Summary Equations {-}

### Grashof Classification {-}

| Equation | Description |
|:---------|:------------|
| $S + L \leq P + Q$ | Grashof condition for continuous rotation |
| $S$ = shortest, $L$ = longest | Identify extreme link lengths |

### Position Analysis {-}

| Equation | Description |
|:---------|:------------|
| $a\cos\theta_2 + b\cos\theta_3 = g + c\cos\theta_4$ | X-component loop closure |
| $a\sin\theta_2 + b\sin\theta_3 = c\sin\theta_4$ | Y-component loop closure |
| $K_1\cos\theta_4 - K_2\cos\theta_2 + K_3 = \cos(\theta_2 - \theta_4)$ | Freudenstein's equation |

### Transmission Angle {-}

| Equation | Description |
|:---------|:------------|
| $\cos\mu = \frac{b^2 + c^2 - f^2}{2bc}$ | Transmission angle from diagonal |
| $f^2 = a^2 + g^2 - 2ag\cos\theta_2$ | Diagonal length squared |

***

## Design Checklist {-}

**For Four-Bar Linkage Design:**

- [ ] Define the motion requirement (continuous rotation, oscillation, path)
- [ ] Apply Grashof's Law to classify mechanism type
- [ ] Verify $S + L < P + Q$ for crank-rocker applications
- [ ] Calculate transmission angle range through full motion
- [ ] Ensure $\mu_{min} > 40°$ for good force transmission
- [ ] Check for toggle positions (dead points)
- [ ] Verify link proportions avoid interference
- [ ] Consider time ratio for quick-return applications
- [ ] Analyze coupler curve if path generation is required
- [ ] Check that mechanism fits within available space

***
